_comment: Quantified pharmacokinetic drug-drug interactions. exposure_factor multiplies the victim drug's AUC/steady-state level: >1 the perpetrator raises it, <1 lowers it. site='clearance' scales CL (t1/2 changes with it), site='bioavailability' scales F (t1/2 unchanged). onset_h is roughly how long the full effect takes to develop (enzyme induction is slow); it is documentation, not modelled. qualitative=true: the source describes a direction but gives no number, so exposure_factor is null and the app only warns. verified=true: the value was checked against the primary document named in source - an SPC or regulator label, the original study's full text (or its abstract, where the note says 'abstract only'), or a registry's posted results - and the note says where. verified=false: no primary could be reached, primaries disagree, or a field is calibrated rather than observed; the note says which. Drug-information aggregators and label mirrors are never a source for a verified value (tests/test_data_provenance.py). onset_h is not part of verification: no source states one, and the note says so. Victims not listed here (levetiracetam, pregabalin, methylphenidate, lisdexamfetamine, ibuprofen, paracetamol) had no quantified PK interaction in the sources reviewed.

interactions.note: US ibuprofen label: lithium Cmin +15 %, renal clearance -19 % (n=11 healthy volunteers, sustained-release lithium). Class: celecoxib +17 % (Lithobid label), indomethacin +30-59 % (Health Canada monographs). onset_h is an estimate; no source states one.

No hydrochlorothiazide-specific number reachable (Jefferson 1979, Crabtree 1991: abstracts say only 'significant'). Class data bracket 1.25: Health Canada 'often a 20 to 40% reduction' in clearance (x1.25-1.67); chlorothiazide plasma +26 % (Poust 1976); clearance -24 % (Petersen 1974).

US label: renin-angiotensin antagonists 'increase steady-state serum lithium concentrations', no number. Healthy men on enalapril: no significant mean change (DasGupta 1992). Hypertensive patients: +36 %, clearance -25.5 % (Finley 1996). The onset and case-report figures previously noted have no reachable source.

Risperdal label Table 18 (Saito 2005, n=12), active moiety AUC ratio 1.3 at 10 mg, 1.6 at 20 mg, 1.8 at 40 mg paroxetine. Spina 2001 (n=10, 4 weeks): +45 %, as also stated by Health Canada. onset_h is an estimate (studies used 4-week phases).

Risperdal label Table 18 (Bondolfi 2002): active moiety AUC x1.4, Cmax x1.5 (EM 663.0/470.0). Spina 2002 (n=10, steady-state levels, 4 weeks): +75 %. onset_h is an estimate; fluoxetine accumulates over weeks.

Risperdal label: carbamazepine (573 mg/day) with risperidone 3 mg b.i.d., active moiety AUC ratio 0.51, Cmax 0.55 after 3 weeks. Only the Czech SPC is qualitative. Ono 2002: 0.55 after 1 week of 400 mg/day; Spina 2000: -71 % cross-sectionally; Schoretsanitis 2016 TDM (n=21) significantly lower.

Grimm 2006 (Br J Clin Pharmacol 61:58) Table 4: ketoconazole 200 mg once daily for 4 days, single 25 mg quetiapine, 12 healthy men, AUC x6.22 (90 % CI 4.93-7.83), Cmax x3.35, CL/F 138 -> 22 L/h, t1/2 2.61 -> 6.76 h. US label Table 17: 6.2-fold; Czech SPC 4.5: 5-8-fold, and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors are contraindicated. Named for the dose actually given, not the registry's 200 mg b.i.d.: the CYP3A4 share of this preset is derived from this study, so it must not also count as an independent back-test pair. Much of the effect is presystemic (half-life rose only 2.6-fold), so applying it to clearance overstates the half-life change. onset_h is an estimate; no source states one.

Grimm 2006 Table 5: quetiapine 300 mg b.i.d. with carbamazepine titrated to 200 mg t.i.d. (600 mg/day; the table header says b.i.d., the design section t.i.d. from day 13) for about 3 weeks, 14 patients, AUCtau-ss x0.13 (90 % CI 0.11-0.17), Cmax-ss x0.20, CL/F 65 -> 483 L/h. Czech SPC 4.5: AUC 'on average down to 13 %', more in some patients. The mechanism with this preset's CYP3A4 share predicts about 0.30 for the registry's carbamazepine 400 mg b.i.d., so it under-predicts this pair about 2.3-fold. onset_h is an estimate; no source states one.

US Seroquel label 12.3 Table 17: phenytoin 100 mg t.i.d. with quetiapine 250 mg t.i.d., '5-fold increase in oral clearance' (exposure x0.2). Czech SPC 4.5: clearance up 'approximately 450 %' (x0.18). Named for the dose given; the registry's phenytoin row for mirtazapine is 200 mg/day. onset_h is an estimate; no source states one.

Remeron label: carbamazepine 400 mg b.i.d. at steady state, n=24 healthy men, average plasma mirtazapine -60 % (clearance about doubled). Czech SPC: -60 %. onset_h is an estimate (the study gave carbamazepine for 21 days).
Remeron label: phenytoin 200 mg/day, n=18, average plasma mirtazapine -45 %. Spaans 2002 (abstract): AUC0-24 576 -> 305 ng*h/mL, -46 %. onset_h is an estimate.
Remeron label: ketoconazole 200 mg b.i.d. for 6.5 days, single 30 mg mirtazapine, n=24 men, AUC +50 %, Cmax +40 %. Czech SPC agrees. onset_h is an estimate.

Sitsen 2000 (abstract): cimetidine 800 mg b.i.d., n=12, mirtazapine AUC0-24 and Css,av +54 %, half-lives unaffected, 'probably as a result of increased bio-availability': site corrected from clearance. Remeron label: AUC more than 50 %. onset_h is an estimate.
Perucca 1994 (n=8): apparent oral clearance 0.40 -> 0.14 mL/min/kg, half-life 51 -> 118 h; US fluvoxamine label: clearance -65 %. Exposure factor = 1/0.35. Czech SPC: AUC about +190 %.

Andersson 1990 (abstract): omeprazole 20 mg once daily, IV diazepam, n=12 healthy men, clearance -27 %. Exposure factor = 1/0.73. Larger at 40 mg/day: -38 % in CYP2C19 extensive metabolisers (Caraco 1995), -55 % (Gugler 1985); none in poor metabolisers.
Andersson 1990 (abstract): cimetidine 400 mg b.d., IV diazepam, n=12, clearance -38 %, half-life +39 %. Exposure factor = 1/0.62. Other doses: x1.49 (1000 mg/day), x1.76 (1200 mg/day, oral diazepam).

Kirch/Spahn: AUC +90 % at steady state (the abstract's +95 % is Cmax). Half-life unchanged (Duchin 1984, Asgharnejad 1988, Kirch 1982), so the effect is presystemic: site changed from clearance to bioavailability. Primaries range x1.26-2.37 (US Inderal label x1.46, Duchin; Reimann 1981 x1.63-1.94).

US fluvoxamine label: MINIMUM (trough) propranolol concentrations rose a mean 5-fold (range 2-17) with fluvoxamine 100 mg/day + propranolol 160 mg/day (CYP1A2). The AUC ratio, which this field means, is not reported and is at most 5.

Segura 2005 (abstract): paroxetine 20 mg for 3 days, n=7 CYP2D6 extensive metabolisers, MDMA AUC0-inf +27 % (clearance -29 %). CYP2D6 contributes up to about 30 % of MDMA metabolism. onset_h is an estimate.

Hagelberg 2010 (n=10): clarithromycin 500 mg b.i.d. for 4 days, oral S-ketamine 0.2 mg/kg, AUC0-inf x2.6, Cmax x3.6, mainly first-pass (half-life 4.2 -> 6.5 h, so partly systemic). Victim was S-ketamine. onset_h is an estimate; no source states one.

Peltoniemi 2012 (n=11): rifampicin 600 mg/day for 6 days, oral S-ketamine AUC -86 %, IV only -14 %; oral F 11 % -> 2 %. Mainly presystemic. Victim was S-ketamine. onset_h is an estimate (full induction in about a week, per review).

Paulsen 1989 (abstract): 12 healthy volunteers, single oral 1 g amoxicillin with or without 1 g probenecid, AUC 'twice as large'. Replaces 1.37 from Craft 1979, children with meningitis on IV amoxicillin in parallel groups. Tubular secretion blocked.
